record.title: Backup bucket soft-delete period is not set, so erased users' dumps may be recoverable past the promised 30 days
record.description: scripts/backup-cloud-run.sh creates the private backup bucket and sets only an age-30 Delete lifecycle rule. It never sets or disables the Cloud Storage soft-delete retention (--soft-delete-duration=0). GCS gives new buckets a default soft-delete window, 7 days for buckets created after the March 2024 change. If that default applies to the live bucket, a dump removed by the lifecycle rule at day 30 stays recoverable for about 7 more days, roughly 37 days after creation. Those dumps hold rows for users who have since erased their data or deleted their account. The in-app notice (DeleteMyData.tsx) and the privacy policy (privacy.html) say backup copies are deleted automatically within 30 days. The mismatch is at most a few days, and the objects are readable only by project principals who hold restore/read rights; the job's service account has objectCreator only. This is a privacy-promise accuracy gap, not an unauthenticated or cross-tenant exposure. The live bucket's soft_delete_policy, and any project-level or organization-level override, cannot be observed from the repository.
record.claimed_root_cause: The bucket-creation and lifecycle configuration in cmd_setup covers only object age. The backup-retention promise in the UI and policy is checked by server/legal.test.ts only against the RETENTION_DAYS constant in the script, so the soft-delete window is not part of the guarantee.

trace.description: User-facing statement that copies in the nightly backups are deleted automatically within 30 days after the user erases data or deletes the account.
Policy states backups are kept 30 days, then deleted automatically, so erased data is gone from backups within 30 days.
Each nightly dump is a full pg_dump of the production database (sessions and verification data excluded) uploaded to the bucket, so it contains the live user data of every account at that time.
gcloud storage buckets create sets only uniform access and public access prevention. It does not set --soft-delete-duration=0, so the platform default soft-delete window applies.

The only expiry control is a Delete lifecycle rule with condition age=30 (built at line 37). Objects it deletes enter the soft-delete state and remain restorable for the soft-delete window, past the 30 days promised.

evidence.description: Lifecycle JSON contains a single Delete rule with age RETENTION_DAYS (30). No soft-delete, versioning, or retention-policy setting appears anywhere in the script (confirmed by grep for soft_delete/soft-delete across the repository: no hits in scripts/ or backup/).
The policy-versus-system test asserts only that RETENTION_DAYS equals 30 and that the policy text says 30 days. It does not check bucket soft-delete, so the gap is untested.
The retention row promises that erased data is gone from backups within 30 days, a firm outer bound that a 7-day soft-delete tail would exceed.

The backup service account holds only roles/storage.objectCreator, so the extra recoverable copies are reachable only by privileged project operators, not by the app or other users. This bounds impact to low.

blockers: The live bucket's soft_delete_policy (retentionDurationSeconds) cannot be observed from source. It may be the 7-day default, 0 if set out of band, or overridden by a project or organization default.
Whether the bucket was created before or after the platform change that made soft delete the default for new buckets is unknown.

validation_plan.local: No local reproduction is possible: this is Cloud Storage behaviour. Source review confirms nothing in the repository disables or sets the soft-delete duration.
validation_plan.deployment: Project owner runs the read-only command `gcloud storage buckets describe gs://$BUCKET --format='value(soft_delete_policy)'` and checks for retentionDurationSeconds greater than 0. If it is non-zero, either run `gcloud storage buckets update gs://$BUCKET --clear-soft-delete` and add `--soft-delete-duration=0` to the create call in cmd_setup, or change the policy and DeleteMyData.tsx wording to 'within 37 days'. Optionally list soft-deleted objects with `gcloud storage ls --soft-deleted gs://$BUCKET` to see the tail. No data is modified by the check.
